verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents its own sandbox backend that runs tool execution to reduce blast radius, with modes, scopes, workspace access and images. The exec tool is bounded by the selected sandbox filesystem, and the architecture is framed as untrusted execution under deterministic policy. One community comment that access is full by default reflects configuration defaults, not a concrete failure of sandboxing, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. missing for 10: detailed documentation of per-tool policies/allowlists and permission modes, evidence that sandboxing is on by default rather than opt-in, VM-level isolation details, independent or hands-on corroboration that the sandbox contains risky runs.

support.subject: As a security engineer, risky tool runs are containable — container/VM sandboxing, tool policies, or permission modes that limit what the agent can touch
